h1: The 7 Best Docking Stations for Chromebooks of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Chromebook Docking Stations: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven docks for Chromebooks, from certified dual-4K units to triple-monitor hubs, compared on display limits and charging.
summary: The Plugable 12-in-1 Chromebook Certified dock is our best overall for anyone who needs dual external monitors. The Plugable UD-MSTH2 gives dual 4K 60Hz without certification, and the Plugable Triple Display is for newer Thunderbolt Chromebooks. The Anker 8-in-1 is the budget choice for ports and a single extra screen.
intro: Chromebooks are the reason most generic docks disappoint. ChromeOS cannot always drive two external monitors from a plain USB-C hub, because many Chromebooks support only one external display over the port. The dock you pick has to either use DisplayLink or match your exact model.

We reviewed seven docks on paper, ranking them on ChromeOS compatibility, display output, charging and ports. Listings differ a lot in what they say about Chromebooks, so we leaned on the stated compatibility lines and owner reports.

products.name: Plugable 12-in-1 Dual 4K USB-C Docking Station (Chromebook Certified)
products.verdict: Chromebook certified, with dual 4K via DisplayLink.
products.description:
The Plugable 12-in-1 is certified for Chromebook, Windows and ChromeOS, and gives dual 4K display via DisplayLink. It charges at 60W and has Ethernet in a 12-in-1 layout.

It ranks first because the Chromebook certification removes the compatibility guesswork that sinks other docks. Against the UD-MSTH2 below, you pay for that certification and the DisplayLink approach. Its price lands between $100 and $200.

Buy it if you specifically need two external monitors on a Chromebook. The caveat is that 60W charging is modest.
products.idealFor: Chromebook owners who need dual external monitors.

products.name: Plugable USB-C Docking Station Dual Monitor 4K 60Hz (UD-MSTH2)
products.verdict: Dual 4K 60Hz via two HDMI ports, driverless on ChromeOS.
products.description:
The UD-MSTH2 offers dual 4K 60Hz over two HDMI ports, 65W charging, gigabit Ethernet and USB-C plus three USB-A 5Gbps ports. It is driverless on Windows and ChromeOS.

It ranks second because it lacks the Chromebook certification of the 12-in-1, though it charges at 65W. The listing falls in the $100-200 bracket.

Choose it for dual 4K without paying for certification. The caveat is that MST-style dual output depends on your Chromebook's USB-C support.

products.name: Plugable USB-C Triple Display Docking Station
products.verdict: Three HDMI outputs and 100W charging for newer Chromebooks.
products.description:
The Plugable Triple Display dock has three HDMI outputs, one at 4K 30Hz and two at 1080p 60Hz. It provides 100W USB-C Power Delivery and six USB 5Gbps ports, and works with Windows, macOS and ChromeOS.

It ranks third because the 4K output is only 30Hz and the full multi-monitor output depends on a newer Thunderbolt-equipped Chromebook. The listing falls in the $100-200 bracket.

Choose it if you own a newer Thunderbolt Chromebook and want three screens. The caveat is the 30Hz 4K limit.
products.idealFor: Newer Thunderbolt Chromebook owners wanting three screens.

products.name: Anker Laptop Docking Station Dual Monitor, 8-in-1 USB C Hub
products.verdict: An 8-in-1 hub with 85W PD for under $100.
products.description:
The Anker 8-in-1 USB-C hub lists dual monitor output through two HDMI ports, 85W Power Delivery, 1 Gbps Ethernet and an SD card reader.

It ranks fourth because it makes no Chromebook claims, so its dual-monitor output may drop to one display on ChromeOS. That puts it in the $50-100 price tier.

Choose it if your Chromebook already supports one external display and you just need ports. The caveat is that dual output is not guaranteed on ChromeOS.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who need ports and one extra screen.
products.skipIf: You need two monitors on ChromeOS.

products.name: Selore Laptop Docking Station 3 Monitors, Triple 4K Display
products.verdict: Triple 4K display with 100W PD at a budget price.
products.description:
The Selore dock is listed for triple 4K display, with three HDMI and two DisplayPort outputs, 100W Power Delivery, 10Gbps USB A and C and gigabit Ethernet. It adds an SD and microSD reader and smart display.

It ranks fifth because it makes no Chromebook claim, though it gives triple-monitor headroom for Thunderbolt Chromebooks. That puts it in the $50-100 price tier.

Choose it for a Thunderbolt Chromebook or a mixed-device desk. The caveat is that your Chromebook must support it.

products.name: USB C Laptop Docking Station Dual Monitor HDMI, 14-in-1 USB C Hub
products.verdict: A 14-in-1 hub packed with ports at the lowest price.
products.description:
This 14-in-1 USB-C hub offers dual HDMI plus DisplayPort output, 100W PD pass-through, four USB-A ports, two USB-C ports, SD and TF readers and audio.

It ranks sixth because it states nothing about ChromeOS, so you must know your Chromebook's display limits. It is the cheapest here. Its price lands between $25 and $50.

Choose it for the most ports at the lowest price. The caveat is that compatibility is your responsibility.
cons: Display limits are yours to check
products.idealFor: Buyers who know their Chromebook's display limits.

products.name: Anker Prime Docking Station, 14-Port with 160W Max Output
products.verdict: A 160W dock that shares a Chromebook with a power-hungry laptop.
products.description:
The Anker Prime is a 14-port dock with 160W max output, 10Gbps data transfer, dual 4K displays and a Real-Time Smart Interface display.

It ranks last because it is overbuilt for a Chromebook alone, though it suits households docking a Chromebook and a higher-power laptop together. The listing falls in the $100-200 bracket.

Choose it if you share one dock between machines. The caveat is that you pay for wattage a Chromebook will not use.
cons: More power than a Chromebook needs
products.idealFor: Households sharing a dock with a higher-power laptop.

whatMatters.detail: Many Chromebooks drive only one external display over USB-C. A certified or DisplayLink dock avoids that limit. Look for 'Chromebook certified' or 'ChromeOS' on the listing.
DisplayLink sends video over USB using a driver, and MST splits one video signal into several. DisplayLink works on more hosts. Check the listing for which one it uses.
Docks charge through the same cable. Chromebooks often need 45W to 65W. Match the dock's PD to your charger rating.
Triple-display docks may cap one screen at 4K 30Hz. That feels laggy for desktop use. Read the per-port refresh rate.
Newer Chromebooks with Thunderbolt can drive more screens. Older ones cannot. Check your Chromebook's spec sheet before choosing a triple dock.

faq.q: Can a Chromebook run two external monitors?
faq.a: Some can through DisplayLink docks like the Plugable 12-in-1. Many only support one over plain USB-C.

faq.q: What mistake do buyers make with Chromebook docks?
faq.a: They buy a generic hub and expect two screens. Check the ChromeOS line first.

faq.q: Is the certified dock worth it over the UD-MSTH2?
faq.a: If you want certainty, yes. The UD-MSTH2 offers 65W and dual 4K 60Hz without certification.

faq.q: Do I need a driver on ChromeOS?
faq.a: The UD-MSTH2 is driverless on ChromeOS. The 12-in-1 uses DisplayLink, which is listed as certified.

faq.q: How do I check my Chromebook's display limits?
faq.a: Look at the spec sheet for its USB-C display support. Match it to the dock.

faq.q: Can I use a triple display dock on any Chromebook?
faq.a: No. The Plugable Triple Display and Selore need a capable, often Thunderbolt, Chromebook.

finalTake: The Plugable 12-in-1 Chromebook Certified dock is the safest dual-monitor choice for ChromeOS. The UD-MSTH2 is the driverless alternative, and the Anker 8-in-1 is the budget hub. Check your Chromebook's display limits before buying anything else.
